lines.text: For one year, I lived alone on a space station.
At least, that's what they told me.
Day one. 250 miles above the Earth, an alarm went off.
Ammonia leak. In Module 3, the other half of the station.
Commander Hale sealed Hatch 3, and said: everyone on that side is gone.
The gauge on the hatch dropped to zero. No air.
Our escape capsule had three seats. One of them had a red tag. No go.
So two could leave. And one had to stay.
Hale looked at me. The next ship comes in 365 days.
Then he handed me a letter.
Three rules.
One. Never open Hatch 3. Not for anyone.
Not even for me.
Two. Every morning, check three numbers. Oxygen. Water. Power.
Three. Talk to Ground only on channel 4. If anything calls on channel 9, don't answer.
Twelve envelopes. One a month. Never early.
Then the capsule undocked, and I watched it fall toward the Earth.
Day two. Ground called on channel 4.
Ground copies. Continue.
Every morning, I checked the numbers.
Oxygen, 312 kilos. Water, 97 percent. Power, 100.
Day thirty. Envelope one.
Write the numbers down. By hand.
So I did. And that's when I saw it.
One person breathes less than one kilo of oxygen a day.
The tank was losing 1.7 kilos. Every day.
As if someone else was breathing my air.
I told Ground. Ground copies. Continue.
Day forty. Three in the morning.
I was asleep, strapped to the wall, when I heard it.
Knock.
Knock.
Knock.
It came from Hatch 3.
From a room with *no* *air.*
